segments.text:
- `Rg(recs)` (line 192) builds the range of the records of the row. It calls `val` (line 176) for each record. It stores the lowest rate, the highest rate, the median, the number of intervals and the number of processes.
- `band` is the range of the 8000 MT/s rows of the block. When it is given, the row gets one note that starts with `!`. `rg.nearest(band)` (line 210) gives the distance of the nearest ends of the two ranges, from the rates before rounding.
- The note is `inside the band` when the lowest and the highest rate of the row lie inside the band. It is `overlaps the band` when the two ranges share a value and the row is not inside.
- In every other case the note gives the distance, rounded to 0.01 GB/s, with the words `higher (right of the band)` or `lower (left of the band)`.
- Line 1707 adds the notes of `more` after the note of the band. The function returns a dictionary with the name, the range `rg`, the marker kind `hollow`, the notes and the label. Without `label` the label is the name.
- Example from the page of the saved build: the row `Part L` of the old read kernel has the note `1.24 GB/s lower (left of the band)`.
segments.heading: Function `p_row`: one row of figure 2

segments.text: Returns the notes of a row without the marks at their start, and with a space in place of each `|` (a line break inside a note). The mark `!` means a bold note. The mark `~` means a note that only repeats a part of the row name. With `tooltip=True` the `~` notes are left out.
segments.heading: Function `plain_notes`: notes as plain text

segments.text: Splits each note at `|` into the lines that the figure draws. Each line carries a flag. The flag is true when the note starts with `!`. `panel` then draws the line in bold type (line 1837).
segments.heading: Function `note_lines`: drawn lines of the notes

segments.text: `F2_GAPS` collects one entry per panel of figure 2. The page check in lines 2812 to 2817 reads it. `HIT_R` is the radius of the hover area of a dot that has no other dot within 24 px: 12 px (pixels, the unit of length on the screen).

- Layout code. It reads no rate.
- It starts with a circle of radius `HIT_R` around dot `i`, as a polygon with 32 corners.
- For every other dot that is less than 24 px away, it cuts the polygon at the line half-way between the two dots. So the hover areas of two dots never overlap.
- The script stops when a hover area has fewer than 3 corners.
- It returns the corners, and a flag that is true when a neighbour cut the circle.
segments.heading: Function `hit_cell`: hover area of one dot

segments.text: Returns the area of a polygon from the coordinates of its corners, in square pixels. Line 1788 calls it for each hover area.
segments.heading: Function `poly_area`: area of a polygon

segments.text:
- `build` calls it twice (lines 2695 and 2698): for the panel `Old read kernel` with `P_OLD_BLOCKS`, and for the panel `Load-only loop` with `P_NEW_BLOCKS`.
- `lo` and `hi` are the axis limits in GB/s. `sx` converts a rate to a horizontal position with a linear scale: the rate `lo` lies at 190 px and the rate `hi` at 450 px.
- `sx` converts the rate to a floating-point number. Only the drawing uses this copy.
- `color` is the colour of the dots of the panel. `build` passes `BLUE` for the old read kernel and `ORANGE` for the load-only loop.
segments.heading: Function `panel`: draws one panel of figure 2

segments.text: Vertical layout. Each block, group and row gets its position `y`, and each row gets its height `h`. The height of a row grows by 13 px per note line. No rate is read here.

- One dot per interval record. `r["rg"].v` holds the rates of the records of the row, as `val` returned them. They stand in the order of `r["rg"].recs`: by launch time, then by interval number (line 197).
- The horizontal position of a dot is `sx` of its rate before rounding. `beeswarm` (line 1682) gives each dot a vertical offset. So dots of one row with near x values do not cover each other.
- Each entry of `r["dots"]` holds the record, x, y and the index of the dot in the panel.
- `gap` is the distance of each dot to the nearest other dot of the panel. The script stops when the smallest distance is 5.2 px or less. 5.2 px is the outer radius of the largest mark while the pointer is on it.
- `hit_cell` builds the hover area of each dot.
- `F2_GAPS` gets one entry for this panel: the title, the number of dots, the smallest distance, the number of hover areas that a neighbour cut, and the areas of all hover areas.

Starts the SVG text of the panel. It writes the head lines: the title, the sub-title, the unit of the x axis, and the sentence that the axis starts at `lo` GB/s and not at 0. Lines 1794 and 1795 explain the text under a row name: lowest to highest rate in GB/s, and the number of intervals.

- Lines 1798 to 1806 draw the grey band of each block that has one. Horizontally the band runs from `sx(b["band"].lo)` to `sx(b["band"].hi)`: the lowest and the highest rate of the 8000 MT/s rows of the block. Vertically it covers the groups whose `band` flag is true.
- The tooltip of the band is the text `band_title` of the block.
- Lines 1807 to 1816 draw the grid lines at the rates `minors` and `majors`, and the numbers of the major lines above and below the rows. Inside a band each grid line is drawn again in a darker tone. A grid line within 3 px of a band edge is not drawn again (line 1815).
- Lines 1817 to 1820 draw the axis line with a break mark, the axis title, and again the sentence that the axis does not start at 0.

- Writes the title bar of each block with its `band_txt` lines, the title of each group with its `sub` lines, and the label of each row.
- Under the label it writes `r['rg'].txt()`, and after it `r['rg'].n` in round brackets: the lowest and the highest rate of the row with 2 decimals, and the number of intervals. Example from the page of the saved build: `461.61 to 464.29 (6)` for part L of the old read kernel.
- Then it writes the note lines. A line of a `!` note is drawn in the colour `INK` and in bold type. Every other line is drawn in the colour `MUTED`.
- Line 1838 draws a thin line under the row.

- Loop over the dots of the row. `cell` is the SVG path of the hover area of the dot.
- `where` names the interval of the dot for the tooltip.
- Part A, row A-3: the number of the process inside its csv file (`_fproc`, set in line 349), the tag, and the interval number counted from 1.
- Part A, every other row: the number of the process inside its csv file, the round, and the interval number counted from 1.
- bwx12: the tag of the process, the round, the position, and the kernel that was timed directly before (`kernel_before`). When no kernel ran before, the text is `no kernel ran before it`. A kernel before that is not oldread, read or asmread gets the words `another test loop of bwx12`.

- `tip` is the tooltip text of the dot. It starts with the row name and the notes of the row (`plain_notes`, without the `~` notes), the kernel name and `where`.
- Then comes the rate of the interval: `f2(val(rec))`, the value of `val` rounded to 0.01 GB/s.
- Then come the range of the row, n as intervals and processes, and the source text of `src` (line 359): the csv file and the line of the interval row. For a bwx12 record the source text ends with the sentence that the rate is the sum of the 120 thread rows after that row.
- Example from the page of the saved build: `Part C, read directly after oldread: read (new read kernel), process T72C1, round 0, position 1, directly after oldread: 320.90 GB/s.`

- Writes the dot: first the invisible hover area with the tooltip, then the painted mark.
- A row with `hollow` true (an 8000 MT/s row) gets a ring of radius 3.4 px in the panel colour.
- Every other row (a 7200 MT/s row) gets a filled circle of radius 4.3 px in the same colour.
- Lines 1861 and 1862 close the SVG text and return it.
Returns the interval length of the first record of a list as text, for example `6 s`. It reads the field `min_ms` (the shortest length of one interval, in ms) and keeps the whole seconds.
segments.heading: Function `secs_txt`: interval length as text

segments.text:
- `pool` is `B_L_OLD` or `B_L_ASM` (lines 291 and 292). For each row L-1 to L-4 it holds the oldread records at position 0, or the asmread records at position 1.
- Each of the four becomes one `p_row` with hollow markers. The label is the row name with the interval length, for example `L-1 (6 s)`.
- No band is passed. So these rows get no note.
segments.heading: Function `l_rows`: rows L-1 to L-4 of figure 2

segments.text: Returns the tooltip text of a grey band: what the band shows, its range `rg.txt()` in GB/s, n, and the sorted names of the csv files of its records.
segments.heading: Function `band_title`: tooltip text of a grey band

segments.text:
- `F72_NOTES` and `CI_NOTES` are the fixed notes of the rows F72d12 and control I.
- `IN_PLACE_2` is a group label in two lines. The script stops unless it equals the label `IN_PLACE` of figure 1 (line 1561).
- Line 1884 stops the script unless both records of `C_ASM_AO` (part C, asmread directly after oldread) come from `crev.csv`, round 1, position 0. The order crev times asmread, read, oldread. So asmread at position 0 of round 1 follows oldread at position 2 of round 0.

- First block of the list: the 0.5 s measurements of part A, binary bw_old, kernel `read`.
- Grey band: `rPA_old` (line 463), the range of the 21 intervals of the rows A-1 to A-3 (`P_A_OLD`, line 304).
- Group `8000 MT/s`: one row for each of A-1, A-2 and A-3 with the records `B_A_OLD[d]` (line 298). Hollow markers, no note.
- Group `7200 MT/s, part A`: one row per session with the records of `A_OLD` of that session. A session has 6 such intervals from 2 processes (round 1 and round 2). Each row is compared with the band.
- `n8000` (line 401) writes n of the band as intervals / processes / 1 boot.
segments.heading: `P_OLD_BLOCKS`: blocks of the panel Old read kernel

segments.text:
- Second block: the 6 s measurements of bwx12, kernel `oldread`. Line 1894 states that the rows L-2 to L-4 are 4 s measurements.
- Grey band: `rPL_old` (line 466), the range of the 11 oldread intervals at position 0 of the rows L-1 to L-4 (`P_L_OLD`, line 296).
- Group `8000 MT/s`: `l_rows(B_L_OLD)`.
- Group `7200 MT/s`: four rows, each compared with the band. They are F72d12 (`F_OLD`, 2 intervals), part L (`L_OLD`, 6 intervals), part C (`C_OLD`, all 8 oldread intervals, at position 0 and at position 2) and control I (`I_OLD`, 4 intervals).
- The row of part L gets a second bold note: the difference of the two medians `L_OLD_MED` (line 490), without its sign, rounded to 0.01 GB/s.
- In the page of the saved build, part L has the notes `1.24 GB/s lower (left of the band)` and `medians: 6.27 GB/s lower`. The saved output holds both values. It prints the first one with its sign, as -1.24 GB/s [Ref5].

- `A_V3[rnd]` (lines 509 to 516) holds two ranges of bw_new `read` for the round. `r7` is the range of the 3 intervals of session 1 at 7200 MT/s. `r8` is the range of the 6 intervals of the rows A-1 and A-2 at 8000 MT/s.
- The grey band of the block is `r8`.
- `rows8`: one row for A-1 and one for A-2, each with the 3 intervals of that round (1 process). Hollow markers.
- `rows7`: one row per session with the 3 intervals of `A_NEW` of that session and round.
- Only the row of session 1 gets `band`. So only session 1 is compared with the band. The rows of sessions 2 and 3 get the note `used for Q1 only (rule V3)`.
- The reading note `how2` of the page states how the sessions differ (line 2689). By this note, sessions 2 and 3 started 5 s after a 120-thread process of part C. Session 1 and the rows A-1 and A-2 did not. Line 2486 stops the script unless the part A steps of sessions 2 and 3 started 5 s after a part C process.
segments.heading: Function `a_new_block`: block of bw_new read, one round

segments.text:
- First block: the 6 s measurements of bwx12. Line 1920 states that the rows L-2 to L-4 are 4 s measurements. Grey band: `rPL_asm` (line 466), the range of the 11 asmread intervals at position 1 of the rows L-1 to L-4 (`P_L_ASM`, line 297).
- Group `8000 MT/s`: `l_rows(B_L_ASM)`.
- Group `7200 MT/s`, asmread in place of the new read kernel, each row compared with the band: F72d12 (`F_ASM`, 2 intervals), part L (`L_ASM`, 6 intervals), part C asmread directly after oldread (`C_ASM_AO`, 2 intervals) and control I (`I_ASM`, 4 intervals).
- Group `7200 MT/s, part C` with `band=False`: four rows without a comparison. Two hold the bwx12 kernel `read` (the new read kernel): directly after oldread (`C_READ_AO`, 4 intervals) and directly after asmread (`C_READ_AA`, 4 intervals). Two hold asmread: directly after read (`C_ASM_AR`, 4 intervals) and as the first interval of a process (`C_ASM_FI`, 2 intervals).
- The label of this group gives the reason: `no 8000 MT/s row of this kind (no band)`.
- Line 1933 adds the two blocks of `a_new_block`, for round 1 and for round 2.
segments.heading: `P_NEW_BLOCKS`: blocks of the panel Load-only loop

segments.text: Reverses the order of the two blocks of `P_OLD_BLOCKS`. The 6 s block of bwx12 then comes first in both panels.
Returns one entry (block, group, row) per row of a block list. By default it leaves out the rows of a group whose `band` flag is false. With `band_only=False` it returns every row.
segments.heading: Function `panel_rows`: the rows of a panel as a list

segments.text:
- `OLD_7200_BELOW`: the names of the 7200 MT/s rows (not hollow) of the panel `Old read kernel` whose range does not overlap the band of their block (`overlaps`, line 207). The script stops unless this list holds only `Part L`.
- `OLD_CMP`: all 7200 MT/s rows of that panel. The script stops unless there are 7 rows and each one has a `!` note with its place relative to the band.
- The 7 rows are the 3 sessions of part A, F72d12, part L, part C and control I.
segments.heading: Assertions for the caption of figure 2

segments.text:
- `NEW_CMP`: the 7200 MT/s rows of the panel `Load-only loop` that have a `!` note. These are the rows that are compared with a band.
- `NEW_7200_IN`: the rows of `NEW_CMP` whose range overlaps the band. `NEW_7200_RIGHT`: the rows whose lowest rate is above the highest rate of the band.
- The script stops unless `NEW_CMP` has 6 rows, only F72d12 overlaps its band, and 5 rows lie above their band.
- Line 1952 stops the script unless these 5 rows are part L, part C asmread directly after oldread, control I, and session 1 of part A in round 1 and in round 2.
- `F2_RIGHT_TXT` is the caption sentence that names these 5 rows.

- `allv_old` and `allv_new`: the rates of all rows of each panel. The part C rows without a band are included.
- `OLD_AX` and `NEW_AX` are the axis limits of the two panels: 458 to 476 GB/s and 276 to 340 GB/s. The script stops unless every rate lies between the limits of its panel.
- `N_DOTS` is the number of dots of figure 2: the number of rates of both panels. The saved build gave 139 dots, and `USED` holds 139 records [Ref5]. A test for this companion confirmed that each record of `USED` is exactly one dot.
Returns the HTML of a legend from a list of entries. Each entry is a symbol and a text.
segments.heading: Function `legend`: HTML of a figure legend

segments.text: Returns a small SVG dot for a legend entry: a ring when `hollow` is true, else a filled circle.
segments.heading: Function `sw_dot`: dot symbol of a legend

segments.text:
- `SW_WHISK`, `SW_BAND` and `SW_PCT` are the legend symbols for the range line, the grey band and the percent text.
- `LEG1` is the legend of figure 1. `LEG2` is the legend of figure 2.
- The legend texts state the encoding of both figures. The colour `BLUE` marks the old read kernel, and the colour `ORANGE` marks the load-only loop. A hollow marker is an 8000 MT/s row, and a filled marker is a 7200 MT/s row.
Start of the table code. `lab` returns a row label for a table cell: the name, and each note on a new line in small type.
segments.heading: Function `lab`: row label with notes

segments.text: Returns the one distinct value of a list. The script stops unless the list holds exactly one distinct value. `q1_table` calls it for a position or a kernel order that must be the same in all records of a group.
segments.heading: Function `only`: the one value of a list

segments.text:
- `build` calls it in line 2736. The inner function `row` builds one table row from an entry of `Q1` (lines 430 to 441). `ds` is the list of the drops of its pairs, in percent (`drops_of`, line 421).
- The cells of the row are: the label, the lowest and the highest drop with 1 decimal (`f1`), the range of the old-kernel intervals of the pairs, the range of the load-only intervals of the pairs, and n.
- `med_rng` is used for the two part A rows only. `pairs` is `A_PAIRS` or `A8_PAIRS` (lines 451 to 455), with one entry per session (or 8000 MT/s row) and round. An entry holds the range of the 3 intervals of the bw_old process (`old`) and of the bw_new process (`new`).
- `med_rng` takes the median of each process and returns the lowest and the highest of these medians with 2 decimals. With `rnd` it uses the processes of one round only.
- `per_round` returns this text for bw_new `read`, once for round 1 and once for round 2.
segments.heading: Function `q1_table`: Table 1, the drop per part

segments.text:
- `a8`: the drops of the rows A-1 and A-2 at 8000 MT/s (`Q1["A8"]`, line 457).
- `pos_ao`, `pos_aa`: the position of the kernel `read` in the two part C groups. `pos_l`: the position of asmread in part L. `ord_ao`, `ord_aa`: the kernel order. It is the csv file name without `.csv` (cfwd or crev). `only` stops the script when the records of a group hold more than one value.
- `where` returns the sessions of the processes of a record group, for example `sessions 1 and 3`. A process without a session number is named `the extra process`.
- Line 2023 stops the script unless each kernel order of part C has 2 processes.

- `rows` is the list of table rows. A text entry becomes a title row that spans all columns. A list entry becomes a row with 6 cells.
- Part C, kernel `read` directly after oldread: `Q1["C_ao"]`. Part C, `read` directly after asmread: `Q1["C_aa"]`. Part L, asmread against oldread: `Q1["L"]`.
- The numbers of pairs (4, 4 and 6) are typed here for the text of n (`n7200`, line 381). Line 438 asserts the same numbers for the pair lists. The process tags in the labels of the two part C rows are typed too (T72C1 and T72C3 in line 2026, T72C2 and T72C4 in line 2027), and no assertion compares them with the records. In the saved build the records of `C_READ_AO` hold the tags T72C1 and T72C3, and the records of `C_READ_AA` hold T72C2 and T72C4 (computed again for this companion).
- Part A: the lowest and the highest of the 6 drops of `Q1["A"]`. Each of them is the drop between the median of the bw_old process and the median of the bw_new process of one session and round (`a_pair`, line 444).
- The two rate cells of part A show process medians, not interval ranges: `med_rng` over the 6 bw_old processes, and `per_round` for bw_new.
- The saved build gave these drops: 30.5 % to 31.2 % (`read` after oldread), 29.7 % to 31.1 % (`read` after asmread), 29.2 % to 30.5 % (part L) and 28.5 % to 31.8 % (part A) [Ref5].

- Rows of the same boot that are not part of the planned rerun: control I (`Q1["I"]`, 4 pairs) and F72d12 (`Q1["F"]`, 2 pairs). The saved build gave 31.9 % to 32.8 % and 35.4 % [Ref5].
- Rows at 8000 MT/s, for context: L-1 (`Q1["L1"]`, 2 pairs), and A-1 with A-2 (the drops `a8` and the process medians of `A8_PAIRS`). The page of the saved build shows 35.9 % to 36.1 % and 33.1 % to 39.8 %.
- The note row says in which sessions each kernel order of part C ran. In the page of the saved build, order cfwd ran in sessions 1 and 3, and order crev ran in session 2 and in the extra process. The note concludes that kernel order and session are not fully separated.
- Table 1 has no row for the 8 asmread pairs of part C. The caption of the table (line 2735) says so. Table 1 also has no row for the 8000 MT/s rows L-2 to L-4. Of the rows L-1 to L-4, `Q1` holds pairs of row L-1 only (line 436).
- Line 2045 returns the HTML table (`table`, line 1501). Its 6 columns are: part and pair, lowest drop, highest drop, old read kernel, load-only loop, n.
Returns the HTML of a note under a table: a first text, then one bullet per further point.
segments.heading: Function `tnote`: note under a table

segments.text: Returns one cell of Table 2: the range `rg.txt()` (lowest to highest rate with 2 decimals), and the text of n under it in small type.
segments.heading: Function `cmp_cell`: range cell of Table 2

segments.text:
- `rC_old_p0`: the range of the part C oldread intervals at position 0. The script stops unless these are 4 intervals, all from `cfwd.csv`, and their range overlaps the 8000 MT/s pool `rPL_old`.
- `C_OLD_P2`: the part C oldread intervals at position 2. The script stops unless these are 4 intervals from `crev.csv`, each directly after the kernel `read`.
- Line 2061: every oldread record of the pool L-1 to L-4 must be at position 0. Every asmread record of the pool must be at position 1, directly after oldread.
- Line 2062 adds one line to the self-check list (`xc_text_range`, line 640). The line is PASS when the range of `rC_old_p0` stands in section 4.2 of FACTS.md, with a tolerance of 0.01 GB/s. The saved build gave 465.54 to 467.83 GB/s [Ref5].
segments.heading: Assertions for the rows of Table 2

segments.text:
- Lines 2064 and 2065: each 7200 MT/s range that the rerun compares with 8000 MT/s must hold only records of the datasets `rerun-A`, `rerun-L` and `rerun-C`. So no record of control I or F72d12 is part of a comparison of the rerun.
- `RERUN_CMP_NEW`: the 4 comparisons of the load-only loop. An entry is true when the lowest 7200 MT/s rate is above the highest 8000 MT/s rate.
- The 4 comparisons are: asmread of part L against the pool, asmread directly after oldread of part C against the pool, and session 1 of part A (bw_new `read`) against A-1 and A-2 in round 1 and in round 2.
- Line 2068 stops the script unless all 4 are true. Lines 2069 to 2072 stop it unless the records of the 4 ranges have these datasets, kernels and session.
- `RERUN_CMP_C = 1` records that one of the 4 is a part C row. Line 2432 uses it.

`T2_RERUN_ROWS` is a text for the caption of Table 2 (line 2751). It names the 4 comparisons of the rerun that sentence 3 of the Short version counts. The number 4 in it comes from `len(RERUN_CMP_NEW)`.

- `build` calls it in line 2752. `pool_l`, `pool_old` and `pool_asm` are label texts for the 8000 MT/s pool L-1 to L-4.
- `pool_l` is the long label of the row `Part C (oldread)` (line 2089). It states that row L-1 has 6 s intervals and ran the argument line of part L. It states that this line differs from the part C lines in the kernel order. It states that the rows L-2 to L-4 have 4 s intervals with other hardware events counted.
- So 2 of the 11 intervals of each pool are 6 s intervals, and 9 are 4 s intervals. Every 7200 MT/s row that is compared with the pool has 6 s intervals (lines 317 to 319).
- The label does not name two more differences of the rows L-2 to L-4. Their processes timed longer kernel sequences: 7 to 15 kernels, against 5 kernels in the part L line. Each sequence starts with oldread, asmread. In round 1 the kernel directly before oldread is read_1pl in the part L line. In the rows L-2 and L-3 it is another test loop. The 3 processes of row L-4 ran 1 round, and the part L line runs 2 rounds. These facts were read for this companion from the `# bwx:` header lines of the 6 csv files of these rows.
- `cannot(rg)` returns the sentence on the difference that an overlap result cannot exclude. The size is `width_pct(rg)` (line 476): the width of the 8000 MT/s range in percent of its lower end, printed with 1 decimal.
- The sentence labels this size as an estimate (`est. from one boot`).
segments.heading: Function `q2_table`: Table 2, 7200 MT/s against 8000 MT/s

segments.text:
- Rows of the old read kernel. Each list entry is one table row with 6 cells: the row name, the 7200 MT/s range with n (`cmp_cell`), the 8000 MT/s range with n, the overlap, the distance of the nearest ends, and the wording.
- In every row of this function the cells `yes`, `no` and `0` are typed. The assertions in lines 486 to 498 and 514 stop the script when a typed result does not hold. The wording cells of 9 of the 12 rows with 6 cells use the fixed texts `WORD_SAME` and `WORD_DIFF` (lines 470 and 471). The other 3 rows have their own text: the two part A rows of bw_new `read`, and the part C row of the bwx12 kernel `read`.
- Part A: `rA_old` (18 intervals of bw_old `read`) against the pool `rPA_old` (21 intervals of A-1 to A-3). The text adds the width of both ranges, and the number of 7200 MT/s intervals below and above the 8000 MT/s range (lines 525 to 528). `one_process` (line 531) names the session and the round of each of these two groups. It stops the script unless a group holds the 3 intervals of one process. In the page of the saved build, the 3 intervals of session 1, round 2 lie below the range, and the 3 intervals of session 3, round 1 lie above it.
- Part C: `rC_old` (all 8 oldread intervals) against the pool `rPL_old` (11 oldread intervals at position 0). The text states that the 8000 MT/s rows hold oldread at position 0 only. It adds the range of the 4 part C intervals at position 0. It states that this range overlaps the pool too (asserted in line 2058).
- Part L: `rL_old` (6 intervals) against `rPL_old`, overlap `no`. The distance `L_OLD_NEAR` (line 489) is the highest part L rate minus the lowest pool rate, a negative value. `signed` (line 224) prints it with its sign and 2 decimals. The text adds the difference of the medians, and both values in percent. The saved build gave -1.24 GB/s [Ref5].
- F72d12 (`rF_old`, 2 intervals) and control I (`rI_old`, 4 intervals): each has its own row against `rPL_old`. They are not pooled with part L.

- Line 2099 is the title row of the load-only rows.
- Part L, asmread at position 1: `rL_asm` (6 intervals) against the pool `rPL_asm` (11 asmread intervals at position 1), overlap `no`. The distance is `DIST["nearest"][0]` (line 504): the lowest part L rate minus the highest pool rate. The saved build gave +12.48 GB/s [Ref5].
- Part A, session 1, one row per round: `v["r7"]` (3 intervals of bw_new `read`) against `v["r8"]` (6 intervals of A-1 and A-2 of the same round), overlap `no`. The distance is `v["near"]` (line 515). The saved build gave +32.75 GB/s in round 1 and +10.37 GB/s in round 2 [Ref5]. Table 2 has no row for sessions 2 and 3 of bw_new `read`. The comment in line 508 names rule V3 for the use of session 1.
- The wording cell of these two rows does not use `WORD_DIFF`. It starts with the typed text `outside (above) the 8000 MT/s range of the same round`. Line 514 asserts this result.
- Then the cell gives the pass counts per interval: the one value of `p7` at 7200 MT/s, and the distinct values of `p8` at 8000 MT/s (line 516). Two typed sentences follow: the counts are not all equal, and part A therefore gives no exact size of the difference.
- No assertion checks the sentence on the pass counts. In the page of the saved build it holds: 664 passes at 7200 MT/s against 600 passes at 8000 MT/s in round 1, and against 600, 603, 663 and 664 passes in round 2.

- Part C, bwx12 kernel `read` (the new read kernel): the two 7200 MT/s ranges `rC_read_ao` and `rC_read_aa`, each with n. The 8000 MT/s cell holds `no bwx12 run`. The overlap cell and the distance cell hold `-`. The text starts with `Insufficient data`: this kernel was never run with bwx12 at 8000 MT/s.
- The position 1 in the name of this row is typed. No assertion compares it directly with the records of `C_READ` (line 283). `q1_table` reads the position of both groups from the records (line 2015). Table 1 of the saved build prints position 1 for both.
- Part C, asmread directly after oldread: `rC_asm_ao` (2 intervals) against the pool `rPL_asm`, overlap `no`. The distance is `rC_asm_ao.nearest(rPL_asm)`. The saved build gave +15.56 GB/s [Ref5]. The text of the row states one mismatch: the 8000 MT/s rows hold asmread at position 1, and this row holds it at position 0. Lines 1884 and 2061 assert both positions.
- Table 2 has no comparison row for the other 6 asmread intervals of part C: the 4 intervals directly after `read` (`C_ASM_AR`), and the 2 intervals that are the first interval of their process (`C_ASM_FI`). Figure 2 shows them in the group without a band (lines 1931 and 1932). The note on the older runner bwx uses `C_ASM_AR` (line 2150).
- F72d12, asmread: `rF_asm` against `rPL_asm`, overlap `yes`. The text gives the width of the pool range in GB/s, and the distance of F72d12 above row L-1 alone (`rL1_asm`, line 467). The saved build gave 1.73 GB/s above L-1 [Ref5].
- Control I, asmread: `rI_asm` against `rPL_asm`, overlap `no`. The saved build gave +4.61 GB/s [Ref5].

- A test of the choice of the pool. `alone` lists the 8 rows that use the pool L-1 to L-4. Each entry holds the 7200 MT/s range, the pool range, and the range of row L-1 alone.
- `changed`: the rows whose overlap result against L-1 alone differs from the result against the pool. The script stops unless this list holds only `F72d12, asmread`.
- `pool_x`: the two pools with the records of X2d12 added. The script stops when an overlap result changes with this larger pool.
- Line 2134 stops the script unless the text of n of X2d12 is the same for both kernels.

- Line 2135 adds the title row `Notes`. Three notes follow, each as one row over the full width of the table.
- Pool or L-1 alone: how many of the 8 rows keep their overlap result (from `alone` and `changed`), and the distance of F72d12 above L-1. The note states that the pool was chosen after the numbers were seen.
- Part C: a fixed text. It says that the rules file contradicts itself on part C. The page compares the two part C rows that have a row in the list of 8000 MT/s rows. The note states that this choice was made after the numbers were seen.
- X2d12: the ranges `rX2_old` and `rX2_asm` (line 1326) and n. The note says that the row is shown and not used.

- The note on the rows of the older runner bwx. The comment in line 2146 states that no wording comes from them.
- Lines 2147 and 2148 take the text of n of the bwx groups. The script stops when n differs between the kernels.
- `sets`: three groups of part C intervals. Each has the range of the bwx rows with the same kernel directly before, and the distance `X_ABOVE` (line 545). The script stops unless each distance is above 0.
- The note lists how the bwx rows differ from part C: the binary, the number of kernels in the sequence, the counter setting and the start option.
- It gives the highest bwx rate of the kernel `read` and of asmread (`X_MAX_READ`, `X_MAX_ASM`, lines 546 and 547). For each set it gives the distance of the part C range above the highest rate of its bwx rows.
- It gives the highest rates of the bwx processes with another kernel order (`X_REV_MAX_READ`, `X_REV_MAX_ASM`, line 549). The note states that this `read` rate lies inside both 7200 MT/s `read` ranges of part C, and that this asmread rate lies inside the 7200 MT/s asmread range of part L. Lines 551 to 553 assert both. The page of the saved build shows 324.36 GB/s (`read`) and 324.98 GB/s (asmread) for these 8000 MT/s processes.

- The note on the three boots with 10 modules. Its text says that no wording comes from them.
- `n10`: the text of n of the asmread records of one boot. The script stops unless it is equal for the two boots of `T10_ASM` (line 1327).
- The note gives the asmread rates of these two boots with 2 decimals, and `T10_APART` (line 1328): the distance of their two medians in percent of the lower median.
- It gives the oldread range of the three boots (`rT10_old`, line 1329) and the width of this range in percent of its lower end.
- By the text of the note, the two boots of `T10_ASM` had the same firmware settings. The third boot had the original settings. The note names this as a limit: the three boots did not differ by the boot alone.

- The rounding note. `ex` holds two distances: F72d12 above L-1 (this table), and the farthest ends of part L and the pool (Table 4).
- For each one it compares the printed distance with the difference of the two rounded rates. The printed distance is computed from the rates before rounding and then rounded to 0.01 GB/s. An example stays in the note only when the two values differ.
- In the page of the saved build both examples stay: 1.73 GB/s and 39.38 GB/s. The differences of the rounded rates are 1.74 GB/s and 39.39 GB/s (computed again for this companion).
- Lines 2180 and 2181 return the HTML table with 6 columns.

- `build` calls it in line 2756. `l_launch` and `i_launch`: the launch times of the part L processes and of the control I processes, from the field `launch_utc` of the oldread records.
- `l_load` and `i_load`: the 1-minute load averages at these launches (field `load1_at_launch`). `i_gap`: the seconds since the end of the previous 120-thread process (`gap_s` of `LAUNCH`, line 879).
- Line 2192 stops the script unless each part L step started 5 s after part A.
- Line 2193 stops the script unless control I and F72d12 started at a load average below 1.0.
- Line 2195 stops the script unless the text of n is equal for asmread and oldread in each visit.
segments.heading: Function `visits_table`: Table 3, visits of the part L line

segments.text:
- One row per visit: F72d12, part L and control I.
- The cells are: the visit, the launch time, the start state, the asmread range, the oldread range, and n per kernel. The launch cell of part L holds the first and the last of its 3 launch times. The launch cell of control I holds its 2 launch times. The two ranges are `txt()` of the `Rg` objects: lowest to highest rate with 2 decimals.
- The start state of F72d12 uses values of the raw-file checks in lines 1117 to 1127: the seconds since the first kernel log line of the boot, and the busiest process of the saved process list. It also gives the load average at launch, from the first oldread record.
- The start states of part L and control I give the load at launch and the highest %CPU of the saved process lists (`L_ENV_MAX`, `I_ENV_MAX`, lines 1134 and 1135). For part L the text gives the lowest and the highest load of its 3 launches. For control I it gives both loads.
- In the page of the saved build, F72d12 started 20 s after the first kernel log line of the boot, at a load average of 0.34. Part L started 5 s after part A, at load averages of 74.05 to 104.52. Control I started at load averages of 0.87 and 0.91, 287 s and 265 s after the previous 120-thread process.
- In the saved build, the process list of F72d12 shows `pr/ttyAMA-1` at 51.6 %CPU [Ref5]. Line 2199 names it a Linux kernel thread. The process lists of part L and control I show at most 0.1 %CPU [Ref5].

- `build` calls it in line 2758. The table has one row per kind of distance: nearest ends, medians, farthest ends.
- The two values of a row come from `DIST` (lines 503 to 507): asmread of part L against the 8000 MT/s pool, and asmread of part L against F72d12. `f2` rounds each value to 0.01 GB/s.
- The saved build gave 12.48 and 18.87 GB/s (nearest ends), 17.61 and 20.54 GB/s (medians), and 39.38 and 26.03 GB/s (farthest ends) [Ref5].
segments.heading: Function `dist_table`: Table 4, three kinds of distance

segments.text:
- `build` calls it in line 2771. No rate is used here. The table holds launch times and 1-minute load averages.
- First group: one row per step of `STEPS` (line 880), from its entry in `LAUNCH`: the first launch, the load at that launch, and the seconds since the end of the previous 120-thread process.
- For a part A step the text gives the number of processes of the session. Line 2225 counts the values of `proc_key` over all part A records of the session, with every kernel included.
- For a part A step the load cell also lists the load at the launch of each `read` process that the page uses (`A_OLD` and `A_NEW` of the session), in launch order.
- Line 2231 stops the script unless the first of these processes has the load of the first launch of the step.
- In the page of the saved build, step T72A1 started at a load average of 0.07. The 9 later steps of the rerun started at load averages of 74.05 to 105.24, each 5 s after the previous 120-thread process. The 2 steps of control I started at load averages of 0.87 and 0.91.
segments.heading: Function `load_table`: Table 6, load average at each launch

segments.text:
- Second group: the earlier rows of the page. Line 2234 adds its title row `Earlier rows shown on this page: launch of every process`.
- F72d12: the launch time and the load of its first oldread record.
- Rows A-1 to A-3 and L-1 to L-4: one load per process (`proc_key`), in launch order. The launch cell holds the launch time of a single process, or the first and the last launch time of several processes. The records are those of the kernel `read` of both binaries (A-1, A-2), of bw_old (A-3), and the oldread records at position 0 (L-1 to L-4).
- The two groups of the older runner bwx: the first and the last launch, and the lowest and the highest load, from the header facts of their processes (`X_POOL_HEAD`, `X_REV_HEAD`, lines 1259 and 1260).
- X2d12: the launch time and the load from `EXTRA` (line 1299). The three boots with 10 modules share one row: the launch times of the first and of the last of the three processes, and one load per process.
- Line 2252 returns the HTML table with 5 columns.

- `build` calls it in line 2739. It writes one title row per block and group of `F1_BLOCKS` (line 1580), and one table row per row of figure 1.
- The cells are: the row name with its notes, the median of the old read kernel, its interval rates, the median of the load-only loop, its interval rates, and the drop.
- Medians and rates are printed with 2 decimals (`f2`). The interval rates stand in the order of `Rg.v`: by launch time, then by interval number.
- `drop_txt` (line 425) gives the lowest and the highest drop of the row with 1 decimal, or one value when both are printed equal.
